title: SLO translation & handoff compact + 6-week risk-sprint plan
content:
Purpose
Short: define a compact (agreement) that translates product-level commitments into measurable SLOs, and run a focused 6-week risk-sprint to remediate top translation gaps.

Context & problem statement
- Product PMs have high-level SLAs or customer promises (uptime, p95 latency, correctness tiers) that are not always actionable for engineering teams.
- Feature teams pick SLOs inconsistently; observability gaps and ownership confusion cause slow remediation.
- We need a repeatable handoff ritual + a short, timeboxed risk sprint to reduce the top 3 cross-team reliability risks per service.

Goals (measurable)
- Produce an SLO translation compact signed by PM + feature-engineering + SRE for 6 pilot services by end of the 6-week sprint.
- Reduce top-3 risk exposure score across pilots by >= 40% (see risk scoring rubric below).
- Close or mitigate telemetry gaps needed to evaluate SLOs for pilots (50% telemetry completion).

Scope
- In: API latency SLOs (p50/p95), availability SLOs (success rate), error budget policy, observability checks (traces, metrics, alerts), and a minimal runbook.
- Out: detailed capacity planning for Dedicated clusters (separate follow-up).

Stakeholders & roles
- SRE lead: Nora Martinez (owner) — run the compact workshop, facilitate sprint.
- PM reps: Priya Kapoor, product-hosted-api — define customer intent and SLA language.
- Feature eng leads: Ethan Liu, Sofia Reyes — implement SLO targets and alerts.
- Observability: Liam O'Connor — metric + dashboard delivery.
- Solutions / CS: Devon Brooks — customer impact input and escalation policy.

Deliverables (week-by-week)
W0 (prep): select pilot services, collect current dashboards/alerts, baseline risk scores.
W1: SLO translation workshop (1.5h) per pilot — output: compact draft (1 page) with target, owner, measurement sources.
W2: Telemetry sprint — fill missing metrics, add trace sampling rules, dashboard skeleton.
W3: Alert & runbook prototype — implement burn/alert thresholds, create minimal oncall runbook.
W4: Risk remediation sprint — one high-priority fix per pilot (latency tail fix, retry/backoff, cache tuning).
W5: Stability validation & rollout plan — synthetic tests, load probes, smoke runs.
W6: Retrospective, compact sign-off, roll-forward plan for org-wide cadence.

Risk scoring rubric (simple)
- Visibility gap (0-5): missing metric or unclear ownership.
- Exposure (0-5): how often SLO violated in baseline month.
- Blast radius (0-5): number of customers/features impacted.
Total risk = sum (0-15). Prioritize highest totals.

Handoff compact (one-page template)
- Customer promise: (copy from PM SLA)
- Measured SLO: metric name, aggregation, window, target (e.g., success_rate over 7d >= 99.5%)
- Measurement source: metric id, trace sample rates, logs bucket
- Owner: service team, pager owner, SRE contact
- Error budget policy: burn actions (page, scale, rollback)
- Observability checklist: dashboards, alerts, synthetic tests
- Runbook pointer: link + minimal steps for triage
- Signatures: PM, Eng lead, SRE lead

Runbook minimum checklist (to ship with compact)
- How to detect: metric + threshold + runbook page link
- First response: triage steps (check traces, replicate with local env), who to page
- Quick mitigation options: rollback, throttling, cache flush, circuit-breaker toggle
- Postmortem owner + timeline if > 1 hour outage

Communication plan
- Weekly sprint sync (SRE + pilots) 30m on Tuesdays.
- Biweekly cross-functional demo (PMs + CS) at sprint midpoint and end.
- Compact publication: Confluence + pinned Slack thread in #sre-ops for each pilot.

Open questions / decisions to resolve in W1 workshop
- Shall we standardize on 7d sliding window vs. 30d for availability? tradeoffs: sensitivity vs noise.
- Error budget actions: automatic scaling vs immediate rollback — authorize which teams can trigger autoscale.
- Telemetry retention: full traces for 72h or aggregate only? cost tradeoff.

Metrics for success (post-sprint)
- Completed compacts signed: target = 6.
- Telemetry coverage % (per pilot): target >= 50%.
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) change for pilot services: target reduce by 30%.
- Risk score reduction: target >= 40% for prioritized risks.

Appendix: quick templates and commands
- Compact template link: (to be attached)
- Sample PromQL/metric names we discussed: api_success_rate{service=~"pilot-a|pilot-b"}, request_latency_p95_ms
- Quick run commands: curl health probe endpoints, synthetic test runner: ./tools/load-probe --target <url> --profile p95-probe

Next steps (immediate)
- Nora: finalize pilot list and invite W1 attendees by EOD Friday.
- Priya: paste SLA snippets for pilots into the compact template before W1.
- Liam: inventory current dashboards and post link in linked_artifacts.

Notes to self (work-in-progress tone)
- Keep the compact intentionally short. Avoid a 10-page SLO doc that no one reads.
- Emphasize observability-first: can't enforce SLOs we can't measure.
- If a pilot chooses an availability target > 99.99, call out capacity implications early.

TODOs (tracked)
- [ ] Build compact template in Confluence (Nora)
- [ ] Create pilot dashboard skeleton (Liam)
- [ ] Add synthetic probe runner to CI for pilots (Ethan)
- [ ] Schedule retrospective + sign-off session (Devon)
